_comment: The FALLBACK for tax cells PwC's guides did not state, and the record of the eight that needed a judgement rather than a parser. rates_pwc.json wins wherever it carries a rate; classify.tax_from_text resolves anything stating one rate plainly; this file covers what is left. Every entry carries the quote it was read from, so the number on the page traces to a string in data.json rather than to anybody's memory.
_convention: A non-resident's rate is the one that actually leaves the transaction. (1) Where the jurisdiction WITHHOLDS at source, that is the number, whatever the eventual assessment. (2) Where a non-resident may ELECT a flat regime, the flat rate. (3) Where two regimes apply with no default a foreign buyer falls into, no number: the word stays. (4) A genuine band that depends on the owner's other income in that country is a schedule, not a rate.

rent.quote: 20% WHT; marginal rate up to 52% inc. USC
rent.why: The 20% is withheld by the tenant or agent under the non-resident landlord scheme. The 52% marginal figure needs Irish residence to reach.
Cedolare secca is elective and open to a non-resident landlord, and 21% beats the bottom of the progressive band.
The lump-sum regime is the one a non-resident landlord uses. 8.5% is the rate below PLN 100k of rent, which is where a single property sits.

rent.quote: 30% WHT on gross OR elect net basis (10-37% graduated rates)
rent.why: 30% on gross is the default for a non-resident. The net-basis election is available but has to be made.

cgt.quote: FIRPTA: 15% WHT on gross; actual tax 0-20% + 3.8% NIIT on net gain
cgt.why: FIRPTA withholds 15% of the gross price at settlement. The eventual assessment can be more or less and is reclaimed or topped up on a return.

_kept_as_words.Brazil.rent: 15% (via Carne-Leao) or 25% WHT - two regimes, and which applies turns on whether the rent is collected through a Brazilian paying source. No default a foreign buyer simply falls into.
_kept_as_words.Mexico.cgt: 25% of gross or 35% of net gain - the seller elects, and which is cheaper depends on the gain. Rule 3.
_kept_as_words.Thailand.cgt: Specific business tax 3.3% or stamp duty 0.5%, plus income tax 5-35% on the gain portion - three components on different bases. Rule 3.
_kept_as_words.United Kingdom.rent: 20% basic / 40% higher / 45% additional - a genuine band, and which one applies depends on the landlord's other UK income. Rule 4.
